item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Tue Oct 13 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Tue Oct 13 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Tue Oct 13 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.description:

item.title: Tattoo Design Workshop — Tue Oct 13, 3:00 PM — SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART
item.description:
Have you always wanted to design your own tattoos, but never known where to find inspiration? Start at the museum! This monthly workshop provides instructions for examining art to find personal meaning inside it, and how to use that meaning to design tattoos based on your own life! Supplies will be provided to design tattoos. Occasional guests from the local tattooing community may be featured to answer questions about tattoo design, tattoo processes, or the fascinating history of tattoos. This group meets on the 2nd Tuesday of every month, excluding holidays and museum closures. The group will meet in the Roehm Family Art-making Studio, located inside the Simpson Center for Education on the 2nd floor of the Eskenazi Museum of Art.
Source: Architecture + Design, Eskenazi Museum of Art, IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Eskenazi School of Art

item.title: The Art of Money: A Student Guide to Financial Wellness — Tue Oct 13, 5:15 PM — KIRKWOOD HALL
item.description:
Join MoneySmarts, Art Remains, andHideout Pressfor an engaging conversation on budgeting, saving, mindful spending, and building healthy financial habits as a student. Learn practical strategies for managing your finances while embracing sustainable and creative approaches to everyday life. Whether you're planning for your next art project or your future goals, this workshop will help you make the most of your resources—both financial and creative.
Source: IU Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design

item.title: It's On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop — Tue Oct 13, 6:00 PM — Global & International Studies Building
item.description:
The It’s On Us: Bystander Intervention Workshop is a 90-minute, audience-driven bystander intervention program that teaches students the skills needed to help in situations involving alcohol and drug use that could lead to a sexual assault. Students practice helping in real-life scenarios and discuss how alcohol and drug use influences a person’s ability to give and get consent to engage in sexual activity with another person.
It's On Us is required for all first-year and transfer undergraduate students. You must attend one session to fulfill the requirement.
Instructions:
Those who arrive more than 5 minutes after the start time will NOT be allowed into the session and will need to attend a different session
If this is your assigned workshop but you cannot attend it in its entirety, please RSVP for a different workshop.
If you have concerns about attending due to personal experiences or need to request accommodations, please contact the office at itsonus@iu.edu.
A

item.title: Union Board presents: Take a Hike! — Fri Oct 16, 12:30 PM — Griffy Lake Nature Preserve
item.description:
Union Board's Out & About and Mind & Body committees are teaming up to get you off campus and onto the trail! We're taking 50 students on a guided hike at Griffy Lake, completely free of charge!
Meet at the IMU Biddle Hotel Lobby at 12:30 PM, where we'll catch a bus out to the trailhead at Griffy Lake Nature Preserve. Two guides from IU Outdoor Adventures will lead the group along the lake trails, point out what's growing and living in the woods around you, and keep the pace easy for everyone. When the hike wraps up, we'll bring you back to the IMU.
No hiking experience needed. Just show up with the right shoes, a water bottle, and a willingness to get a little muddy!
Hosted by: Indiana Memorial Union Board, IU Outdoor Adventures
Additional Information can be found at: https://beinvolved.indiana.edu/event/12794581
Source: IU beINvolved Student Orgs

item.title: Embedded Counseling (CAPS) — Mon Oct 19, 8:00 AM — LGBTQ+ CULTURE CENTER
item.description:
Supporting your well-being is an important part of our work at the LGBTQ+ Culture Center. That's why we are proud to partner with Counseling & Psychological Services (CAPS) to provide an embedded counselor in our space every Monday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Mollibeth Penner, LHMCA serves as our embedded counselor and works directly with students connected to the LGBTQ+ Culture Center. item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. item.title: Augmented Humanity: How Human–Agent Teams Will Change the Way We Solve Problems — Tue Oct 20, 4:00 PM — 701 E Kirkwood Ave
item.description: ABOUT What we call artificial intelligence is really aggregated, harnessed human intelligence, like a library or a civilization. What's new is the harness, and who holds it. Since the spring of 2026, Peter Kaminski has worked every day with a small team of personal AI assistants: long-lasting agents with names, memory, and bounded autonomy, which work for him alone and keep all their memories and working files on his own machine, on his premises. (Their thinking power still comes from the cloud; he'll be exact about what that does and doesn't expose.) Pete makes the case that people and their agents, working together and with other people and their agents, will change the way we solve problems. item.title: BOOK SHARE: THIS MAGNETIC NORTH — Wed Oct 21, 4:00 PM — Juniper Art Gallery
item.description:
About the Book: What happens when a place is so beautiful that everyone wants to go there—and then they stay?
This book explores a phenomenon occurring around Michigan’s Great Lakes and other high-demand scenic locations across the country: natural landscapes are undergoing profound human and climatological change as people pick up their lives and move to bucolic locations. The Grand Traverse region in northwest lower Michigan has been one of the most impacted regions in the state, with the population increase accelerated by the pandemic and climate change. The impact of this growth is explored through field observations and interviews involving dozens of born-and-raised locals, 'boomerangers' (those who grew up, left, then returned), and relocators. The author explores the tensions between newcomers and 'natives.' Interviewees include tourist industry leaders, conservationists, business owners, public safety officials, tribal members, Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore officials,

This exhibit highlights the student experience and the multitude of ways students found a sense of home, identity and belonging at Indiana University.
Source: IU Bloomington Libraries
